_comment: Weather. A spell lasts a few waves and shifts every tower and enemy on the board at once, so it changes what a build is WORTH without changing the build -- which is the one thing a difficulty multiplier cannot do. `effects` are plain multipliers where 1.0 is neutral.
_trade_comment: Every type is a trade, never a pure penalty. Rain costs range but slows what is walking through it; hot sun boosts damage but cooks the reload; fog is nearly all cost but pays a little accuracy back. Weather that is only ever bad is a difficulty slider with a different name, and the player would just wait it out.
_visual_comment: `tint` and `alpha` drive a full-board translucent wash, and `particles` picks the falling/drifting art. Both are deliberately restrained: the wash has to be visible without hiding the lane, so alpha stays under 0.12 and the particles do the identifying.
_timing_comment: first_wave keeps the opening clear so weather cannot decide the first few waves, where the game is at its most knife-edge. Spells last min_waves..max_waves waves, and `clear` is in the pool with real weight, so calm stretches happen on their own rather than being special-cased.

types.name: Clear
types.description: Nothing in the air but the fighting.

types.name: Rain
types.description: Wet air shortens effective range and slows the reload, but the ground turns to mud under everything walking on it.

types.name: Snow
types.description: Drifts bog the lane down badly, but the cold stiffens every mechanism on the board.

types.name: Sleet
types.description: The worst of both: half-frozen ground slows the enemy, and ice in the workings slows you more.

types.name: Hot sun
types.description: Clear air and long sight lines sharpen every hit, but the heat cooks the reload and the enemy moves with the shade.

types.name: Thunderstorm
types.description: The charged air puts real force behind every shot, and squall lines cut the range badly.

types.name: Fog
types.description: You cannot see what you are shooting at, so range collapses -- but at the distances left, every shot tells.
